newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila sees public sector surplus in 1997, 1998.
newsitem.headline: Manila sees public sector surplus in 1997, 1998.

text.p: The Philippines is projecting higher public sector financial surpluses in calendar 1997 and 1998, according to documents issued by the finance department on Thursday.
The consolidated public sector finances include that of the national government, the Central Bank, government-owned and controlled corporations, state pension funds and financial institutions.
The country registered a 2.5 billion peso surplus between January 1 and December 10, 1996.
The finance department said it was expecting a 4.31 billion peso surplus for 1997, up from the original balanced position, because of a higher fiscal surplus to be posted by the government.

A 17.91 billion peso surplus was expected in 1998, up from an earlier estimate of 15.63 billion pesos, mainly due to lower costs in restructuring the Central Bank, the documents said. ($1 = 26.3 pesos) -- Manila newsroom 63 2 8418938, Fax 8176267
